parsed.explanation: Explicit trans-specific criminalisation dominates: Article 521 allows up to six years for 'men disguising as women', reaching trans feminine presentation, with documented police arrests, a 36-person raid, intrusive anal examinations and activist arrest. Article 534 remains in force despite favourable appellate rulings, and prejudice/violence is rising in the capital. Courts have provided real mitigation by freezing the 2022 gathering ban and questioning Article 534, and no execution or custodial killing is documented, raising it above the most severe tier, but imprisonment for presentation itself is credible and remedies are incomplete.

entry_documents.exposure: Article 521 criminalises trans feminine presentation and documentation barriers are documented; entry screening and marker treatment of visitors specifically is not sourced.
entry_documents.protection: A 2015 judge approved one marker change and courts have reviewed such requests, but legal gender recognition is recorded as not available and settled practice is uncertain.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/presentation mismatch could be treated under Article 521; no documented visitor border procedure confirms or refutes this interaction.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented police arrests of LGBT people, intrusive anal examinations ordered by prosecutors, a 36-person 2012 cinema raid, and arrest of an activist pressuring Pride cancellation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented custodial placement, beating or lethal custody regime; appellate courts have repeatedly declined to apply Article 534 to consensual conduct.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under morality/presentation provisions creates detention and extortion/humiliation risk, though duration and conditions in custody are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Explicit and de facto criminalisation of transgender expression, particularly trans women; Article 521 up to six years and Article 534 up to one year remain on the books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2009, 2017 and August 2023 rulings held consensual relations not unlawful; court practice has moved against Article 534 without repeal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Retained statutes plus documented raids and activist arrest show enforcement despite judicial mitigation; current prosecution rate after 2023 is unsourced.

minors_guardians.interaction: No documented age-specific rule; a guardian's presentation could expose the travelling party to the same criminalisation, but this is not sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Rise in prejudice and violence against trans and queer people documented in the capital, including incidents responding to a decriminalisation bill; police rather than protection are documented actors in raids and arrests.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National administrative court froze the June 2022 interior-minister ban on LGBT gatherings in November 2022 as inciting violence and violating rights.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Judicial freeze limits executive bans, but street hostility and police-initiated crackdowns remain operative, especially around public LGBT events.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Articles remain in force, arrests and examinations documented, and whether Article 534 is still applied after August 2023 is unresolved; facilities and visitor police treatment are unsourced unknowns.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning appellate and administrative courts have ruled against prosecutions and frozen the gathering ban, showing remedies sometimes work.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies mitigate executive and Article 534 action but do not remove Article 521 exposure or prevent police arrests; absence on visitor procedures is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar explicit presentation criminalisation with routine police arrests, but unlike 0.15-A there is no documented months-long custody with beatings, illusory courts, or capital provision; appellate courts here have actually ruled against prosecution and frozen a ban, so rating is higher than 0.15.

Closest anchor: morality provision applied selectively, undercover/blackmail risk, appellate annulments, fines or short jail and no capital outcome. This case adds a six-year trans-specific presentation statute and documented anal examinations, suggesting a similar or slightly lower score.

0.35-B involves hours-long identity-check detention and fines but seldom imprisonment. Here imprisonment up to six years for presentation, a 36-person raid and intrusive examinations are documented, so the case is materially below 0.35 despite real judicial remedies.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national criminal law targeting trans feminine presentation is the operative exposure, amplified by police raids, activist arrest and rising capital violence. Appellate and administrative courts provide partial, documented mitigation for same-sex conduct and assembly, but do not repeal the statutes or prevent arrests, and visitor-specific border, facility and care rules are undocumented. For an outed visitor, especially a trans woman, arrest and imprisonment are credible; execution and lethal custody are not documented, placing the case in severe/high risk but above the catastrophic tier.
